newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Electric to join international call market.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Electric to join international call market.

text.p: Japanese electronics and machinery maker Mitsubishi Electric Corp said on Wednesday that it plans to enter the international phone call market as early as 1998.

A wholly owned subsidiary, Mitsubishi Electric Information Network Corp, will offer international calls by connecting Mitsubishi Electric's phone lines to public phone networks in Japan and overseas, a spokesman for Mitsubishi said.
Currently, companies other than existing international call carriers are not allowed to offer such services.

However, in October, the government began allowing companies which lease lines from long-distance carriers for their internal needs to offer public call services via those lines, and it is poised to expand the deregulation to international calls by the end of next year.
The liberalisation is expected to promote competition and bring down the cost of phone calls.

Mitsubishi Electric, which is involved in industrial machinery, data communications systems and consumer electronics, said last month that it would start a domestic long-distance call service next May to take advantage of the deregulation.
